prompt: Which value of $x$ is **not** a solution to $7 - 2x \ge 1$?
hint: Solve the inequality first, then see which choice falls outside the solution set.

hints.text: Solve the inequality first, then see which choice falls outside the solution set.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a simpler one: which value fails $5 - x \ge 2$? Solving gives $x \le 3$, so $x = 4$ fails. Solve first, then test the choices against the solution set.
Every choice at or below $3$ works, so the one that fails is $4$.

learningObjective: Solve an inequality and identify a value outside the solution set.
explanation: Divide by $-2$ and flip the inequality: $x \le 3$.
Choices A, B, and C are all at most $3$ and therefore work. Choice D, $x = 4$, is greater than $3$ and fails: $7 - 2(4) = -1$, which is not $\ge 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Skip solving and just substitute
steps: With only four numbers to check, plugging in is often faster than solving.
This also sidesteps the sign-flip rule entirely — the single most common error on inequality questions.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Solving perfectly and then choosing a value that IS a solution — the word NOT reverses the final selection.
Find the solution set first, write it down (x ≤ 3), then pick the choice OUTSIDE it. Two separate acts, in that order.
